IronMac from Cradle to PE [6258]

By: Floris Kotze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The death of a friend spurs Mac to do above and beyond expectations

Unique Selling Point:
This will NOT be a typical CB insert. We will have 2 x presenters on this one. Derek gets a peek into the suffering and sacrifices of Mac's Ironman training.
What is Ironman, and what led Mac to tackle this monumental challenge.


Summary:
We see what it takes to do an IronMan. Derek, together with Mac, takes us on an emotional journey as to the reason Mac is doing it. We meet various people on this journey including Mac’s training partner and coach.

Further information:
Mac is tackling Ironman in honour of his friend, André. We see Mac cycling and training in the Cradle. André was cycling on the very same road Mac is.
Derek speaks to André’s wife. We hear about the dangers cyclists face in the country.
Many cyclists have lost their lives because of reckless drivers. This has to stop.

IronMac.

We open up the piece with very jovial athletes, smiles and hugs, sweaty athletes that won a race. Definite triumphant vibes, they have conquered.
Podiums, prizes and sacrifices.
Then a few voxies that says, “to do Ironman is no joke!”.
We see Derek chatting and encouraging athletes…
We realize they are doing a triathlon… training for Ironman!
We still don’t know what it really means… but we know it is one of the toughest events on the athlete's calendar…

Then…

We see Mac crossing the finish line of the Joburg Ultra Triathlon in the Cradle of humankind….
Derek asks how he is doing.
He is elated, very tired but elated. We have no idea what is going on… but we stay with Mac as he says…
“To find out why I am here, we have to go back to the beginning of the year…”
Editing in this section is faster paced.
The above section is roughly 01min30 secs

Fade to black…

Audio
“Reports of an accident…”, “cyclist killed”, ‘accused in court’, ‘drunk driving’
We cover this with Mac. He is alone. In a dark Room. He looks straight into the camera…

Breaking the fourth wall he says:
“I have decided to do Ironman. I’ll tell you why…”
He goes on to tell us the story.
He explains what happened to Andre Piehl, his friend.
We suddenly see a different side to Mac.
We stay on his face.
He is emotional.
We now understand why he is doing Ironman…
He is not only doing it for Andre, but for all cyclists,
Cyclists killed all over the country by reckless drivers….
(This takes us to the next scene)
Editing in this section is medium/slow paced.
The above section is roughly 01 Min







Scene of the Crime (Mac and Derek)
Derek and Mac walks along a road.
Mac explains to Derek what he saw on that day, driving past his friend André’s accident scene. Although he did not know it at the time, that moment would change Mac’s entire life.
We understand now how close they were. Mac mention Sharon and his kids, to link us to our next scene. Derek can mention that we are going to talk to her perhaps.
The above section is roughly 01 Mins

Sharon Piehl (Andre’s Wife)

Derek rings a bell, a woman opens up, they walk into the house. We see them walking past family pictures…
Then we realize it is Andre’s wife, Sharon.
Derek and Sharon have a very emotional sit down.
Sharon shares with Derek the heartache and the grief.
She shares André’s legacy and tells us about the #cyclistslivesmatter campaign
Derek explains to her what Mac’s aim is… to do Ironman, and Derek says Mac is training hard as we speak…
(Links us to the next scene)
The editing in this section is elegant, respectful and gentle and slow paced.

The above section is roughly 02 Mins 30 secs

Coach
We see Mac is training hard! Running and cycling…
We meet Mac’s coach. Derek and his coach is chatting, perhaps Mac can join in…
His coach talks to us about the race. But also mentions the deaths of athletes he knew.
It is hard. Reality hits home.
Mac trains in the background.
We get a Rocky Philadelphia Museum of Art stairs vibe…
Mac breaks the fourth wall now and again to let us into his frame of mind…
He is tired. We feel it. The editing pace is fast and so is the music.
His coach says he has many training events…
Editing in this is fast paced.

The above section is roughly 02 Mins 00 secs










Fade from Black
Title on-screen:
Cradle Race - 04 December 2022 05:12AM

We fade to Mac getting ready for a race.
We drive with him. He is quiet. Now and again he says something. He is nervous.
He briefly tells us where we are going…
He gets to the venue. Derek meets him there…
It is a bit chaotic.
Editing pace picks up. It is a bit frantic. Rushing to get things done. He puts his bicycle in the transition zone, putting on a number, tying shoes.
Then silence…. Everything is slomo.

We hear nothing… then, BANG!

The start gun goes off and they rush into the water.
We spend time with Mac as he completes the race…
Derek cheered him on.
Now we remember what happened at the start,
He crosses the finish line again….
Tired, he reminds us again why he is doing this….

For the fallen athletes.

The above section is roughly 02 Mins 00 secs






Extra Budget Items:
I would like Derek to go and support Mac whilst doing a training event in the Cradle. It is on a Sunday, the 4th of December.

Case Study:
Sharon Piehl Wife of André

Expert:
Mr. Mac Molele
Mr. Gugu Masina Coach

https://pedalpower.org.za/

Locations:
Cradle of humankind

Script:


Chaos, noise, excitement…
“Ladies and Gentleman, good morning to you and welcome to the beautiful Cradle Moon venue…”
Montage
Runners, etc.
Derek Link
Over the years we’ve told the stories of many extraordinary people from all walks of life and today is no different. We’re in the Cradle of humankind, supporting one of our own.
VO:
It is almost 7 O'clock on a warm Sunday morning in December. Mac is getting ready to tackle a half Ironman. That means, a 1.9km swim, a 90 kilometre cycle and a 21 kilometre run.
Derek: I detect a slight bit of nerves?
Mac: Slight?! I'm very nervous about it but I just want to get to the finish. I'm not here for times, nothing, I just wanna get to the finish line.
VO:
At this point you probably wonder: why is Mac doing a half IronMan, and what is so special about that…. Well, that is exactly what this story is about…
Mac Studio:
One day I was driving towards Lanseria Airport and as I looked I saw that there was a lady that was sitting on the floor, and she was holding a gentleman or someone in her hands, but I could see it is a cyclist, and she was rocking this person, and I could almost see that this man's scalp had almost been removed, and I'm guessing that's where the helmet was, and the impact on us to remove the skin off, so I could, because I could almost see his head, and it totally freaked me out.
VO Effects
A very very sad thing happened, a driver’s accused running over two cyclists, killing one…
A cyclist was killed by an alleged drunk driver near Lanseria…
Mac Studio:
A week later I see a Facebook post, and it's Sharon, Sharon Piehl. And Sharon I've known for the past 15 to 20 years, and so I see her post it says my dear Andre, taken from us too soon to know your memory live… and I'm like as I'm reading this, I'm now adding one and one, and I'm, and then I'm like oh God, that person that was hit by car that day was Andre, Sharon's husband!
Sharon:
I said goodbye like I would every other day and walked back to my room and phone rang and, it's, they just said, just come quickly and helicopters were there, in my mind I am going, maybe he is in the helicopter or he is in one of the ambulances… but he wasn't.
VO:
Andre left quite an impression on Mac. He was an exceptional triathlete, he represented South Africa in the world champs, and Sharon, his wife, and biggest supporter, always by his side…
Sharon:
Just that instantaneous tragedy that just ripped your entire life within 30 minutes. I was speaking to him 30 minutes later it was over.
Mac:
I always tease André, I said to him, why are you doing Ironman, what is wrong with you? And I said to him, you know what, when I'm old and stupid enough like you, I'll do Iron Man.
I am doing this Iron Man in honour of André, in honour of his memory, his kids, his wife…
Sharon:
It's an incredible gift that you can leave that somebody was impacted by André’s life and that, that light continues to shine through. That's why for me, it is something that I absolutely celebrate and applaud, because I'm going, that's what is so important, it is how André lived this life.
Qondisa:
We reached out when the Andre Piehl incident happened, to the to department of Transport, and we've been engaging with them ever since. The idea is to form a task team, that is going to look at how we are going to improve the safety of cyclists on the road.
Qondiswa Intro
Cycling South Africa’s president Qondisa Ngwenya, a keen cyclist himself, has been at the helm of the organisation since the beginning of the year.
Qondisa: I am very, very concerned about it, I think particularly in the last 18 months since my involvement in the leadership of cycling, we've seen some horrific accidents on the road happening across the board.

Derek: Can we put a number on the deaths or incidents involving cyclists every year?

Qondisa: Yeah the latest figures I saw was 451 fatalities per annum, I mean that is a horrific number, I think that is just the reported cases, the number is most probably much higher than that.
VO:
Despite all the dangers, Mac, like so many other cyclists, has to head out on the road everyday.
It is mid November, and Mac’s been hard at work for just over 2 months. I catch up with him on the road.
Derek:
How's the training going?
Mac: The training is going well. I think this week for the first time my body is not in pain, but for the past sort of like 6 weeks, everything's been sore, even my nails, I think even my hair has been sore!
Mac:
Our training officially began on the 1st of October, but the 1st of November is almost where we now been kicking everything off, training six days a week spending time in the pool, time on the bike, time on the road. Every single day right up until Iron Man. Everything is in pain, but, I think it's going to be worth it at the end of the day and hopefully we will make it over there to the finish line.
Langa:
15 Seconds…
Mac:
Langa has been running almost all his life, has been cycling all his life, he's done the comrades about six times, so, I thought, you know they let me do this with someone that I like, somebody that I get along with, and somebody that I know.
VO:
Having grown up together, Langa Lloyd Marlowe knows Mac well. Conditioning Mac for the Ironman in March, is his top priority.
Langa:
It is a mammoth challenge, to do an Ironman takes a lot of sacrifice. Mostly in terms of your time, you looking at least about 10 hours on the bike per week, that you have to spend away from family, and you have to run at least about 50 Ks within that week so that's another 5 hours and you have to put in the swim, and you have to sustain it over at least an 18-week period.
The biggest thing is really about consistency, and just keep on waking up in the early morning, and turning up for training and doing it over and over again.
Mac:
The minute I get onto a bike, the first thing that comes is, you know, do I have my helmet on, are all my lights on? Because sometimes it starts cycling very early in the morning. You almost ride that bike with a prayer, that's all you do. At any point in time, somebody can skip a robot. You constantly got to have your situational awareness, because if you don't, it can cost you your life…
Neil
South Africans live in a Lawless society. We don't obey the law. Part of my role is working with the government to try and bring about long-term change, to make sure we don't have these incidents where people lose their loved ones.
VO:
Neil Robinson is the CEO of Pedal Power Association. Operating out of Cape Town and have been in the forefront of promoting cycling in South Africa. Following Andre's death they launched a project called “#cyclistslivesmatter” with one goal in mind, making our roads safer for all cyclists.
Derek:
Neil, Mac taking on the Ironman in Andre’s name, does that help to focus on cycling and safety?
Neil:
Absolutely and every little bit helps. I think it is a wonderful gesture in memory of Andre. All these things help and they add to the pressure that we're building on the unlawful nature of, and the absolute tragedy of these kinds of things that happen on our roads every single day.
Mac is another step closer to fulfilling his promise to André. At the Joburg Ultra Triathlon, Mac’s endurance was pushed to the limits.
He experienced many difficulties. Problems with his wetsuit meant he could only do half the
swim, and tyre issues meant he had to cut the cycling too.
The harsh reality is: Ironman is double the distance!
Despite missing the cut-off, Mac pushed ahead with the final discipline and completed the run.
This is the farthest distance he has done in one day, spending over 9 hours on his legs!
Mac:
I think Andre spirit just keeps us going, one one foot in front of the other, I just kept on saying, I must finish, I must finish, I must finish, so I don't want to let him down, I don’t wanna let the kids down, and I don’t want to let Sharon down… more than anything else, I don’t want to let myself down. I just want to see this through.
Sharon
I hope that what the campaign does is, the promise to Andre inspires other people to also take on their biggest challenges and that, that light continues. Mac will learn that he will cry every time he crosses that finish line.
Derek: There will be tears…
Sharon: There will be tears, from pain or just from pure exhilaration, and just what you've managed to achieve. If Mac is being inspired by André to do IronMan, then, you know, what a great gift to me and my children.
Derek Link:
The entire Carte Blanche team, if not the whole country is behind you Mac, and remember what Andre used to say: “Leave it all on the road”.

Promo1: 11”
South Africa has a long way to go to prevent the deaths of cyclists on our roads. We speak to experts desperate to ensure their safety.

Promo 2: 21”
It’s a challenge very few of us would be willing to take on…
Upsound:
We follow Mac as he trains for Ironman in Honour of a friend and fellow cyclist mowed down on the road.
Promo 3: 21”
Mac’s life changed in an instant when he witnessed the death of a friend and fellow cyclist
Upsound:
Too many cyclists have lost their lives on our roads, is anything being done about it? We speak to the experts.

Mac: The minute I get onto a bike, the first thing that comes is, you know, do I have my helmet on, are all my lights on? Because sometimes it starts cycling very early in the morning. You almost ride that bike with a prayer, that's all you do. At any point in time, somebody can skip a robot. You constantly got to have your situational awareness, because if you don't, it can cost you your life… Neil South Africans live in a Lawless society. We don't obey the law. Part of my role is working with the government to try and bring about long-term change, to make sure we don't have these incidents where people lose their loved ones. VO: Neil Robinson is the CEO of Pedal Power Association. Operating out of Cape Town and have been in the forefront of promoting cycling in South Africa. Following Andre's death they launched a project called “#cyclistslivesmatter” with one goal in mind, making our roads safer for all cyclists. Derek: Neil, Mac taking on the Ironman in Andre’s name, does that help to focus on cycling and safety? Neil: Absolutely and every little bit helps. I think it is a wonderful gesture in memory of Andre. All these things help and they add to the pressure that we're building on the unlawful nature of, and the absolute tragedy of these kinds of things that happen on our roads every single day. Mac is another step closer to fulfilling his promise to André. At the Joburg Ultra Triathlon, Mac’s endurance was pushed to the limits. He experienced many difficulties. Problems with his wetsuit meant he could only do half the swim, and tyre issues meant he had to cut the cycling too. The harsh reality is: Ironman is double the distance! Despite missing the cut-off, Mac pushed ahead with the final discipline and completed the run. This is the farthest distance he has done in one day, spending over 9 hours on his legs! Mac: I think Andre spirit just keeps us going, one one foot in front of the other, I just kept on saying, I must finish, I must finish, I must finish, so I don't want to let him down, I don’t wanna let the kids down, and I don’t want to let Sharon down… more than anything else, I don’t want to let myself down. I just want to see this through. Sharon I hope that what the campaign does is, the promise to Andre inspires other people to also take on their biggest challenges and that, that light continues. Mac will learn that he will cry every time he crosses that finish line. Derek: There will be tears… Sharon: There will be tears, from pain or just from pure exhilaration, and just what you've managed to achieve. If Mac is being inspired by André to do IronMan, then, you know, what a great gift to me and my children. Derek Link: The entire Carte Blanche team, if not the whole country is behind you Mac, and remember what Andre used to say: “Leave it all on the road”. Promo1: 11” South Africa has a long way to go to prevent the deaths of cyclists on our roads. We speak to experts desperate to ensure their safety. Promo 2: 21” It’s a challenge very few of us would be willing to take on… Upsound: We follow Mac as he trains for Ironman in Honour of a friend and fellow cyclist mowed down on the road. Promo 3: 21” Mac’s life changed in an instant when he witnessed the death of a friend and fellow cyclist Upsound: Too many cyclists have lost their lives on our roads, is anything being done about it? We speak to the experts.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The death of a friend spurs Mac to do above and beyond expectations
metadata.Unique Selling Point: This will NOT be a typical CB insert. We will have 2 x presenters on this one. Derek gets a peek into the suffering and sacrifices of Mac's Ironman training. What is Ironman, and what led Mac to tackle this monumental challenge.
metadata.Summary: We see what it takes to do an IronMan. Derek, together with Mac, takes us on an emotional journey as to the reason Mac is doing it. We meet various people on this journey including Mac’s training partner and coach.
metadata.Further information: Mac is tackling Ironman in honour of his friend, André. We see Mac cycling and training in the Cradle. André was cycling on the very same road Mac is. Derek speaks to André’s wife. We hear about the dangers cyclists face in the country. Many cyclists have lost their lives because of reckless drivers. This has to stop. IronMac. We open up the piece with very jovial athletes, smiles and hugs, sweaty athletes that won a race. Definite triumphant vibes, they have conquered. Podiums, prizes and sacrifices. Then a few voxies that says, “to do Ironman is no joke!”. We see Derek chatting and encouraging athletes… We realize they are doing a triathlon… training for Ironman! We still don’t know what it really means… but we know it is one of the toughest events on the athlete's calendar… Then… We see Mac crossing the finish line of the Joburg Ultra Triathlon in the Cradle of humankind…. Derek asks how he is doing. He is elated, very tired but elated. We have no idea what is going on… but we stay with Mac as he says… “To find out why I am here, we have to go back to the beginning of the year…” Editing in this section is faster paced. The above section is roughly 01min30 secs Fade to black… Audio “Reports of an accident…”, “cyclist killed”, ‘accused in court’, ‘drunk driving’ We cover this with Mac. He is alone. In a dark Room. He looks straight into the camera… Breaking the fourth wall he says: “I have decided to do Ironman. I’ll tell you why…” He goes on to tell us the story. He explains what happened to Andre Piehl, his friend. We suddenly see a different side to Mac. We stay on his face. He is emotional. We now understand why he is doing Ironman… He is not only doing it for Andre, but for all cyclists, Cyclists killed all over the country by reckless drivers…. (This takes us to the next scene) Editing in this section is medium/slow paced. The above section is roughly 01 Min Scene of the Crime (Mac and Derek) Derek and Mac walks along a road. Mac explains to Derek what he saw on that day, driving past his friend André’s accident scene. Although he did not know it at the time, that moment would change Mac’s entire life. We understand now how close they were. Mac mention Sharon and his kids, to link us to our next scene. Derek can mention that we are going to talk to her perhaps. The above section is roughly 01 Mins Sharon Piehl (Andre’s Wife) Derek rings a bell, a woman opens up, they walk into the house. We see them walking past family pictures… Then we realize it is Andre’s wife, Sharon. Derek and Sharon have a very emotional sit down. Sharon shares with Derek the heartache and the grief. She shares André’s legacy and tells us about the #cyclistslivesmatter campaign Derek explains to her what Mac’s aim is… to do Ironman, and Derek says Mac is training hard as we speak… (Links us to the next scene) The editing in this section is elegant, respectful and gentle and slow paced. The above section is roughly 02 Mins 30 secs Coach We see Mac is training hard! Running and cycling… We meet Mac’s coach. Derek and his coach is chatting, perhaps Mac can join in… His coach talks to us about the race. But also mentions the deaths of athletes he knew. It is hard. Reality hits home. Mac trains in the background. We get a Rocky Philadelphia Museum of Art stairs vibe… Mac breaks the fourth wall now and again to let us into his frame of mind… He is tired. We feel it. The editing pace is fast and so is the music. His coach says he has many training events… Editing in this is fast paced. The above section is roughly 02 Mins 00 secs Fade from Black Title on-screen: Cradle Race - 04 December 2022 05:12AM We fade to Mac getting ready for a race. We drive with him. He is quiet. Now and again he says something. He is nervous. He briefly tells us where we are going… He gets to the venue. Derek meets him there… It is a bit chaotic. Editing pace picks up. It is a bit frantic. Rushing to get things done. He puts his bicycle in the transition zone, putting on a number, tying shoes. Then silence…. Everything is slomo. We hear nothing… then, BANG! The start gun goes off and they rush into the water. We spend time with Mac as he completes the race… Derek cheered him on. Now we remember what happened at the start, He crosses the finish line again…. Tired, he reminds us again why he is doing this…. For the fallen athletes. The above section is roughly 02 Mins 00 secs
metadata.Extra Budget Items: I would like Derek to go and support Mac whilst doing a training event in the Cradle. It is on a Sunday, the 4th of December.
